newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election bill faces final Senate vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election bill faces final Senate vote.

text.p: A bill which would allow Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year was due to be put to a second and final vote in the Senate later Wednesday, an official said.
"We expect the vote to take place this afternoon, at about 1700 local time/1600 EDT/2000 GMT said the official, a spokesman in the Senate.
There was, however, a possibility that left-wing opposition parties might succeed in getting a high court injunction to stop the vote.
The parties asked the Supreme Federal Tribunal Tuesday to suspend the vote pending investigations into allegations that members of the Chamber of Deputies were paid to vote for the re-election bill.
"We've not heard of any injunction being granted, so everything's going ahead as normal," the spokesman said.
The constitutional amendment requires a three-fifths majority, equivalent to 49 of the Senate's 81 members, to be approved. In a first vote in May, 63 senators voted in favor of the bill.

If approved in today's scheduled vote, the bill would require only symbolic confirmation in a joint session of Congress to become law. It would also allow state governors and city mayors to stand for a second consecutive term.
